neighbours.label: physical properties of stars in astrophysics text: surface, magnetic field, emission and spin of a star (magnetars, hot stars)
fire: The young star has an unusually strong magnetic field for its size.
Astronomers estimate the star's surface temperature at 20,000 kelvin.
The pulsar rotates hundreds of times a second and beams radio waves.
Hot gas is pulled from the companion's surface onto the white dwarf.
Magnetars are neutron stars with the strongest magnetic fields known.
Dark spots on the star's surface rotate in and out of view.
Blue giants burn hot and shed material in powerful stellar winds.
The flare released energy stored in the star's twisted magnetic field.
quiet: The young plant has an unusually strong root system for its size.
Engineers estimate the engine's surface temperature at 400 kelvin.
The drill rotates hundreds of times a second and cuts through steel.
Hot water is pumped from the boiler onto the floor heating pipes.
Magnetic locks are used on doors that need to open in a fire.
Dark spots on the kitchen surface come from spilled coffee.
Blue paint dries quickly and sheds flakes in strong winds.
The repair released air stored in the tyre's twisted inner tube.

notes: Card: ' magnetic', ' surface', 'osph', ' star' in stellar astrophysics. Probes: star with magnetic field and hot surface 1.25, neutron star emitting pulses 1.08; the same words about a fridge or a table 0.01.
